title: The binary entropy inequality for $f_k$
statement:
For $k\geq2$, let $\psi_k$ be the unique real root of $(1-x)^k-x$ in $[0,1]$, set $\varphi_k=1-\psi_k$ and $\alpha_k=\varphi_k^{k-1}=\frac1{\varphi_k}-1$, and define the extended binary entropy function $h$ and

$$
r_k(x)=h(x^k),\qquad s_k(x)=x^{k-1}h(x),\qquad f_k(x)=\alpha_k r_k(x)-s_k(x).
$$

**Binary entropy inequality conjecture.** The function $f_k(x)$ is nonnegative on $[0,1]$.
The case $k=2$ was proved by Boppana and by AHS using differential calculus, with interval arithmetic also used in the latter proof. The assertion for general $k$ is left as a conjecture in the supplied text.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.12276

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2023). “As mentioned earlier, this was proved shortly after by several researchers.”
source_name: Raphael Yuster, “Almost k-union closed set systems”, arXiv:2302.12276 (2023).
